\subsection{AdaptiveSpanAttention (\texttt{adaptive\_span\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_adaptive\_span\_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Adaptive Span Attention (Sukhbaatar et al., 2019).  Mathematical Formulation:     1. Query-Key Attention Scores:        \$\$S\_{ij} = \frac{Q\_i K\_j^\top}{\sqrt{d}}\$\$          2. Dynamic Per-Head Span Masking:        Let \$z\_h = \sigma(\text{logit}\_h) \cdot S\_{\max}\$.        \$\$M\_{ij}^{(h)} = \begin{cases
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization & SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/adaptive\_span\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{adaptive\_span\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{AdaptiveSpanAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{adaptive\_span\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.7 Implementation \& System Notes}
The module \texttt{adaptive\_span\_attention} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. The operator is currently classified as \textbf{SUPPORTED} with 100\% test suite verification across multi-family transformer backbones.

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Banded Local + Global Context}: Retains dense local syntactic interactions while routing global anchor tokens.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Eliminates low-magnitude and low-sensitivity parameters with minimal task loss.

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Irregular Memory Gather Overheads}: Fine-grained unstructured sparsity may incur GPU warp divergence.
    \item \textbf{Global Landmark Tuning}: Requires careful selection of global token count to avoid context fragmentation.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Format Conversion}: Matrix conversion to CSR/BCSR formats adds minor pre-processing latency.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.7 Implementation \& System Notes}
The module \texttt{aegis\_hybrid} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. \end{itemize}

\subsection{AegisAttention (\texttt{aegis\_v5})}
\label{sec:app_module_aegis\_v5}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
AEGIS-Attention V5 multi-head hybrid module.  Divides \$H\$ heads into \$H\_l\$ local window heads and \$H\_g\$ global RFF linear heads. Projections are low-rank factorized via truncated SVD.  Complexity:     - Local Attention: \$\mathcal{O}(B \cdot H\_l \cdot N \cdot W\_{\text{local}} \cdot d\_h)\$.     - Globa
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization & SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/aegis\_v5.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{aegis\_v5} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{AegisAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{aegis\_v5} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}

\subsection{BAMUMoEBlock (\texttt{bam\_umoe})}
\label{sec:app_module_bam\_umoe}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
BAM Unified Mixture of Experts Attention Block.  Replaces standard linear attention projections and feed-forward networks with parameter-efficient top-k conditional computation blocks with full self-attention and pretrained weight copying.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts & Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/bam\_umoe.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{bam\_umoe} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{BAMUMoEBlock}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{bam\_umoe} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).

Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{CosformerAttention (\texttt{cosformer})}
\label{sec:app_module_cosformer}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Cosformer Attention Layer.  Mathematical Formulation:     1. Non-negative kernel mapping:        \$\$\phi(x) = \operatorname{ReLU}(x) \quad \text{or} \quad \operatorname{ELU}(x) + 1\$\$          2. Cosine-based positional reweighting:        \$\$R(i, j) = \cos\left(\frac{\pi(i - j)}{2 M}\right) = \cos\lef
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 4: Kernelized & Spectral Attention
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/cosformer.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{cosformer} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{CosformerAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{cosformer} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\phi(x) &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} \left[ \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_1 x), \dots, \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_m x) \right]^\top, \\
M &= \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top V_i \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d_v}, \quad Z = \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top \mathbf{1} \in \mathbb{R}^m, \\
O_t &= \frac{\phi(Q_t) M_t}{\phi(Q_t) Z_t + \epsilon}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N m d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N m)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly linear in $N$ via positive feature mapping $\phi(x)$, enabling streaming $O(1)$ state updates.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Positive Orthogonal Random Features (FAVOR+)}: Provides unbiased estimation of softmax attention without negative values.
    \item \textbf{Linear Autoregressive Inference}: Re-orders computation via associativity $\phi(Q) (\phi(K)^\top V)$ for $\mathcal{O}(1)$ step decoding.
    \item \textbf{Frequency-Domain Spectral Mixing}: Projects token sequences into Fourier frequency spaces for global mixing.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Feature Map Variance}: Small feature dimension $m$ can exhibit higher approximation variance on sharp attention distributions.
    \item \textbf{Normalization Instability}: Requires small $\epsilon$ stabilization in the denominator $(\phi(Q) \sum \phi(K)^\top + \epsilon)^{-1}$.
    \item \textbf{Orthogonal Resampling Overhead}: Periodic resampling of projection matrices $\omega$ is required during long training.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{cur\\_moe} operator implements an optimized track 3: mixture-of-experts \& dynamic routing within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts & Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/cur\_moe.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{cur\_moe} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{CurMoe}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{cur\_moe} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models & Recurrent Scans

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{decay\_linear\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}

\subsection{EATBlock (\texttt{eat})}
\label{sec:app_module_eat}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Efficient Attention Transformer (EAT) Attention Module with Progressive Token Pruning.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization & SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/eat.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{eat} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{EATBlock}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{eat} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Bidirectional Factorised Matrix State Recurrent Linear Attention.  Mathematical Formulation:     1. Multi-Head Normalized Projections:        \$\$Q = X W\_q, \quad K = X W\_k, \quad V = X W\_v\$\$        \$\$\tilde{q} = \text{RMSNorm}(Q), \quad \tilde{k} = \text{RMSNorm}(K) / \sqrt{d\_k}\$\$     2. Bidirectiona
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models & Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/factorised\_matrix\_state.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{factorised\_matrix\_state} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{FactorisedMatrixState}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{factorised\_matrix\_state} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}

\begin{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Zero-Footprint KV Cache}: Maintains a compact recurrent state $h_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}$ without unbounded memory allocation.
    \item \textbf{High Parallel Scan Throughput}: Trains with $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ parallel scan depth on GPU Tensor Cores.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Recurrent State Horizon}: Very long associative horizons may require explicit decay gating to prevent historical interference.
    \item \textbf{Non-Causal Task Adaptation}: Requires bidirectional scan passes for non-causal masked language modeling tasks.
    \item \textbf{CUDA Kernel Specialization}: High performance requires customized fused scan Triton/CUDA implementations.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{FASAAttention (\texttt{fasa})}
\label{sec:app_module_fasa}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
FASA: Frequency/Variance-Aware Sparse Attention. Inherits directly from MixAttentionMoSKA with full [CLS] token protection and variance-based pruning.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization & SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/fasa.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{fasa} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{FASAAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{fasa} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

The module \texttt{fasa} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration.     \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.7 Implementation \& System Notes}
The module \texttt{full\_attention} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. \subsection{FusedSVDLinear (\texttt{fused\_svd\_kernel})}
\label{sec:app_module_fused\_svd\_kernel}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
RESEARCH SOTA: Fused SVD-Linear Module. Combines low-rank projection \$Z = x V^T\$, in-SRAM RMSNorm, and up-projection \$Y = Z U^T + b\$ into a single kernel invocation, eliminating HBM roundtrips.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 4: Kernelized & Spectral Attention
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/fused\_svd\_kernel.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{fused\_svd\_kernel} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{FusedSVDLinear}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{fused\_svd\_kernel} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\phi(x) &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} \left[ \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_1 x), \dots, \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_m x) \right]^\top, \\
M &= \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top V_i \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d_v}, \quad Z = \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top \mathbf{1} \in \mathbb{R}^m, \\
O_t &= \frac{\phi(Q_t) M_t}{\phi(Q_t) Z_t + \epsilon}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N m d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N m)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly linear in $N$ via positive feature mapping $\phi(x)$, enabling streaming $O(1)$ state updates.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\label{sec:app_module_fusion\_attn}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
FUSIONATTN: Hybrid Sparse Attention with Block Gating and Subspace Estimation.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization & SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/fusion\_attn.py}

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{fusion\_attn} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}

Gated Linear Attention (GLA) Bidirectional Module.  Mathematical Formulation:     For input sequence \$X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\$:     1. **Multi-Head Projections:**        \$\$Q = X W\_q, \quad K = X W\_k, \quad V = X W\_v, \quad Z = X W\_z\$\$        \$\$\phi(Q) = \text{ELU}(Q) + 1, \quad \phi(K
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization & SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/gated\_linear\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{gated\_linear\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{GatedLinearAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{gated\_linear\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{hamming\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\

\end{align}

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{linformer\_attention} is formulated as:

S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\

\label{sec:app_module_lola\_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
LoLA: Low-Rank Linear Attention with Sparse Caching.  Mathematical Mechanism:     Combines factorized low-rank projections with selective multi-system cached retrieval:     \$\$\begin{aligned}     Q \&= \text{LowRankLinear}\_Q(X), \quad K = \text{LowRankLinear}\_K(X), \quad V = \text{LowRankLinear}\_V(X)
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts & Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/lola\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{lola\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{LoLAAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{lola\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Dynamic Router Load Balancing}: Dispatches tokens adaptively using softmax routing with auxiliary entropy regularization.

\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}

    \item \textbf{High VRAM Memory Footprint}: Requires sufficient GPU memory to host all $E$ expert parameter matrices simultaneously.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Mamba (\texttt{mamba})}
\label{sec:app_module_mamba}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Gated State Space Model (Mamba) Linear Layer Module.  Implements a gated selective state-space projection that acts as a lightweight, linear-complexity alternative to Multi-Head Attention.  Mathematical Mechanism:     Given input :math:`X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}`:      .. math::
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models & Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/mamba.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{mamba} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{Mamba}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{mamba} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Recurrent State Horizon}: Very long associative horizons may require explicit decay gating to prevent historical interference.
    \item \textbf{Non-Causal Task Adaptation}: Requires bidirectional scan passes for non-causal masked language modeling tasks.
    \item \textbf{CUDA Kernel Specialization}: High performance requires customized fused scan Triton/CUDA implementations.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{MambaInject (\texttt{mamba\_inject})}
\label{sec:app_module_mamba\_inject}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{mamba\\_inject} operator implements an optimized track 2: state-space models \& recurrent scans within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models & Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/mamba\_inject.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{mamba\_inject} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{MambaInject}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{mamba\_inject} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Input-Dependent Selective Filtering}: Dynamically modulates continuous state decay $\bar{A} = \exp(\Delta A)$ conditioned on input tokens.
    \item \textbf{Zero-Footprint KV Cache}: Maintains a compact recurrent state $h_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}$ without unbounded memory allocation.
    \item \textbf{High Parallel Scan Throughput}: Trains with $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ parallel scan depth on GPU Tensor Cores.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Recurrent State Horizon}: Very long associative horizons may require explicit decay gating to prevent historical interference.
    \item \textbf{Non-Causal Task Adaptation}: Requires bidirectional scan passes for non-causal masked language modeling tasks.
    \item \textbf{CUDA Kernel Specialization}: High performance requires customized fused scan Triton/CUDA implementations.
\end{itemize}

The module \texttt{mamba\_inject} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. \subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
MinimalAURORA: Energy-Preserving SVD-Factorized Attention.  Mathematical Mechanism:     Retains standard scaled dot-product attention while replacing dense projections     with energy-truncated low-rank factors:     \$\$\begin{aligned}     Q \&= \text{FactorisedLinear}\_Q(X) \\     K \&= \text{Factorised
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity & Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/minimal\_aurora.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{minimal\_aurora} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{MinimalAURORAAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{minimal\_aurora} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}

    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{MinimalSVDAttention (\texttt{minimal\_svd})}
\label{sec:app_module_minimal\_svd}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
MinimalSVD: SVD-Factorized Low-Rank Projection Attention for Transformers.  Mathematical Mechanism:     Compresses attention projections using truncated singular value factorizations     while maintaining full quadratic attention:     \$\$\begin{aligned}     Q \&= \text{FactorisedLinear}\_Q(X) \\     K
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity & Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/minimal\_svd.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{minimal\_svd} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{MinimalSVDAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{minimal\_svd} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{MixAttentionMoSKA (\texttt{mixattention\_moska})}
\label{sec:app_module_mixattention\_moska}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
MixAttention-MoSKA: Frequency/Variance-Aware Sparse Attention (FASA). Prunes key-value tokens based on variance importance while strictly protecting [CLS] (index 0).
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts & Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/mixattention\_moska.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{mixattention\_moska} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{MixAttentionMoSKA}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{mixattention\_moska} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.

\end{itemize}

\subsection{MoBAAttention (\texttt{moba\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_moba\_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context Modeling.  Mathematical Mechanism:     Partitions the sequence into blocks of size \$B\_{\text{sz}}\$ and routes each query block     to top-\$k\$ key-value blocks based on centroid cosine affinity:     \$\$\begin{aligned}     \bar{Q}\_i \&= \frac{1}{B\_{\text
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts & Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/moba\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{moba\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{MoBAAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{moba\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{NativeHybridAttention (\texttt{nha\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_nha\_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{nha\\_attention} operator implements an optimized track 5: structured sparsity \& pruning within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity & Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/nha\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{nha\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{NativeHybridAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{nha\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{nha\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Global Landmark Tuning}: Requires careful selection of global token count to avoid context fragmentation.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Format Conversion}: Matrix conversion to CSR/BCSR formats adds minor pre-processing latency.
\end{itemize}

Positive Orthogonal Random Features:        \$\$\phi(x) = \frac{\exp\left(x W^\top - \frac{\|x\|^2}{2}\right)}{\sqrt{m}}\$\$        where \$W \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d}\$ is an orthogonal random projection matrix (\$W W^\top \approx I\$).
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity & Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/performer\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{performer\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{PerformerAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{performer\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{ProjectionFactorizedAttention (\texttt{projection\_factorized\_attn})}
\label{sec:app_module_projection\_factorized\_attn}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Projection Factorized SVD Linear Attention.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization & SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/projection\_factorized\_attn.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{projection\_factorized\_attn} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{ProjectionFactorizedAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{projection\_factorized\_attn} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

Args:     config: Model configuration specifying `hidden\_size`, `num\_attention\_heads`, and `dropout`.     num\_kv\_heads: Number of compressed key-value heads (\$H\_{kv}\$).     router\_temp: Temperature scaling factor \$\tau\$ for soft routing soft
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts & Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/qcqa\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{qcqa\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{QCQAAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{qcqa\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{RALALinearAttention (\texttt{rala\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_rala\_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Rank-Augmented Linear Attention (RALA) Mechanism.  Augments standard kernel-based linear attention (\$\mathcal{O}(N)\$) with a low-rank parametric correction matrix \$U\_h V\_h^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{d\_k \times d\_k}\$ (rank \$r \ll d\_k\$) to mitigate the capacity bottlenecks of standard low-rank kernel approx
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity & Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/rala\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{rala\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{RALALinearAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{rala\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{ReGLAAttention (\texttt{regla\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_regla\_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Refined Gated Linear Attention module (ReGLA).  Args:     config: Model configuration specifying `hidden\_size` and `num\_attention\_heads`.     rank: Rank parameter (for compatibility with BaseAttention).     kernel\_size: Kernel window width for local depthwise 1D convolution.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models & Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/regla\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{regla\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{ReGLAAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{regla\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.

\subsection{Replace (\texttt{replace})}
\label{sec:app_module_replace}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{replace} operator implements an optimized track 1: low-rank factorization \& svd projections within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization & SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/replace.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{replace} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{Replace}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{replace} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}

Masked Intra-Cluster

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{routing\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\

\end{align}

\subsection{SOAFusedAttention (\texttt{SOAFusedAttention})}
\label{sec:app_module_SOAFusedAttention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Fused SOA Attention module factorizing Q/K/V projections with low-rank bottlenecks.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization & SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/SOAFusedAttention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{SOAFusedAttention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{SOAFusedAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{SOAFusedAttention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{squeezing\_heads\_distill} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Multi-Head Attention with SVD-Factorized Projections, Kernel Linear Attention, and Data-Dependent Exponential Decay Gating Recurrence.  Supports: - Mode "exact": Low-rank projections with exact \$\mathcal{O}(N^2)\$ softmax attention. - Mode "linear" (with `use\_decay\_gating=False`): Low-rank projection
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models & Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/svd\_linear\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{svd\_linear\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{SVDLinearAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{svd\_linear\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}

    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{DecayGatedLinearAttention (\texttt{svd\_linear\_decay})}
\label{sec:app_module_svd\_linear\_decay}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Decay Gated SVD Linear Attention.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization & SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/svd\_linear\_decay.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{svd\_linear\_decay} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{DecayGatedLinearAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{svd\_linear\_decay} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{SvdProjAttn (\texttt{svd\_proj\_attn})}
\label{sec:app_module_svd\_proj\_attn}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{svd\\_proj\\_attn} operator implements an optimized track 1: low-rank factorization \& svd projections within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization & SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/svd\_proj\_attn.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{svd\_proj\_attn} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{SvdProjAttn}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{svd\_proj\_attn} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}

Args:     model: Target PyTorch neural network module.     target\_sparsity: Structured pruning target sparsity ratio \$\rho \in [0, 1)\$.     target\_rank: Low-rank decomposition rank \$r\$.     method: Compression meth

    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/template\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{template\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{YourCustomCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{template\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\label{sec:app_module_test\_all\_attentions\_team}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{test\\_all\\_attentions\\_team} operator implements an optimized track 5: structured sparsity \& pruning within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity & Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/test\_all\_attentions\_team.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{test\_all\_attentions\_team} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{TestAllAttentionsTeam}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{test\_all\_attentions\_team} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

    \item \texttt{d_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).

\subsection{TestSyntax (\texttt{test\_syntax})}
\label{sec:app_module_test\_syntax}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{test\\_syntax} operator implements an optimized track 1: low-rank factorization \& svd projections within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization & SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/test\_syntax.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{test\_syntax} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{TestSyntax}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{test\_syntax} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

The module \texttt{test\_syntax} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration.
